notes: Multiple sources confirm a Friday fry; Travel Wisconsin says finalist for best fish in Marathon County. Menu references Fisherman's Platter and Poor Man's Lobster (usually cod). Some directories list 184060 WI-153, Eland - likely the same building under rural renumbering.

Small-town bar, owner cooks. Friday fry is a big draw: cod, haddock, perch, bluegill plus shrimp combos. CITY AMBIGUOUS: Restaurant Guru and WiscoBars say Elderon (715-454 is the Elderon exchange), Yelp says Wittenberg 54499. Confirm before geocoding.
Six-digit address is Marathon County rural numbering with an Aniwa mailing address - worth confirming. Reviews specifically praise the Friday-night fish fry. Species not sourced.

Six-digit address plus the 715-446 Hatley exchange indicate Marathon County with an Aniwa mailing address. Friday fry lists cod, haddock, walleye, plus jumbo and breaded shrimp. Tuesday Mexican and Saturday steak/lobster specials.
Village of Eland is Shawano County, right on the Marathon line. Dining room advertises a Friday Night Fish Fry; baked cod and a 'Poor Man's Fish Fry' are the standouts. Serving window not sourced.

Restaurant, motel, ballroom and bowling lanes. Own site publishes a Friday Special menu: fried or baked haddock $10.75-$13.00, fried walleye $12.00-$13.00, haddock-and-chicken combo $13.00; potato choice, coleslaw, rye bread. A secondary source mentions lake perch - verify. Already in WPR's Lenten guide.
Just over the Marathon line. Tavern League listing explicitly names a Friday Fish Fry. Country bar on the snowmobile/ATV trail; TLW SafeRide provider. Species not sourced.
Near the Marathon line. Multiple review sources cite Friday fish fries; no first-party menu found. Species not sourced.

Bar/restaurant plus cabins on Pike Lake, the largest lake in Marathon County - distinct from Hatley Hangout, Lisa's at Lakeside and The Red Retriever. Haddock fry is a listed favorite. Call to confirm the fry is currently running.
Diner-style family restaurant; directories list Fish Fry as a category and reviewers praise the baked haddock. FRIDAY-SPECIFIC DAY NOT CONFIRMED - verify before publishing.

This is the Galloway venue - six-digit address is Marathon rural numbering, 715-454 is the Elderon/Galloway exchange, Wittenberg mailing address. One reviewer calls it 'the best place to go in Galloway.' Formerly Jen & Tonics. Menu shows a fish sandwich but no Friday fry confirmed.

On Hwy 153 between Hatley and the Bevent/Norrie area. Tavern League listing; passed a Marathon County health inspection Jan 2025 so it has a licensed kitchen. Known for pulled-pork pizza; no Friday fry confirmed. Older listings show 6484 WI-153.

THE Bevent-area tavern - Bevent Drive, Town of Bevent, Hatley mailing address. In business since 1969. Directory listings only; no menu or fry confirmation. Bevent has essentially no other licensed tavern online, so this is the one to call for that community.
A second Ringle tavern distinct from Clubhouse/Hillside. Cocktails and bar games, no food menu published, no fry mentioned. Some listings give 169845 Brickyard Dr - verify.
On the Ringle/Weston line - Yelp and Yellow Pages say Ringle 54471, delivery platforms say Weston. Menu includes a fish filet and Thursday tacos but no Friday fry confirmed.
Bar and grill with taxidermy, pool tables, horseshoe pit. Known for the Lotsa Mottza pizza. No fish fry mention found anywhere - needs a call.
Cash-only and explicitly allows outside food, which usually signals a drinks-only tavern with no kitchen - likely no fry, but included for completeness as one of only two bars in Elderon village.
